text:
Alex R: Heads up — we need to secure GPU capacity in ap-southeast1 for the new cluster bring-up next Tuesday. Target reservation: 16 A100-80GB equivalent, plus a small V100 pool for legacy workloads. Who can own the quota requests?
Priya S: I can take point on the GCP quota forms today. Do we have the final project IDs and billing contact? @finance please confirm billing account attachment.
Mateo C: I'll post the quota checklist. Quick notes: request both global 'GPUs (all regions)' if you want flexible fallback, AND regional 'GPUs (ap-southeast1)'. Also request the specific machine type limits (e.g., `n1-standard-32` if using that) and TPU/PD limits if needed.
Jenna L: For bring-up validation we'll need 2 validation nodes up for stress testing, and one small replica to test failover. Can we reserve + tag them so autoscaler doesn't steal them?
Li W: Yes — use a reservation plus a label like `bringup-reserve=true`. For GCP: `gcloud compute reservations create bringup-reserve --zone=ap-southeast1-a --resources=accelerator_type:NVIDIA_TESLA_A100,count:8 --specific-reservation` — create 2 reservations (a/b).
Alex R: Perfect. Priya, once you file the request, please include this exact reservation plan and the label scheme. Include cost estimate so SRE and Finance can pre-approve.
Priya S: Filing now. Draft payload: region=ap-southeast1, totalA100=16, totalsV100=4, reservations=2x8, reserveLabels=[bringup-reserve:true], expectedStart=2026-03-24, expectedDuration=30d. Posting the GCP quota ticket link when created.
infra-ops-bot: Reminder: quota requests typically take 48-72 hours for GCP. Use 'accelerated quota review' if it's urgent.
Mateo C: Also add persistent disk IOPS and snapshot quota — our CI creates large images during validation. IOPS bump request: +10k for the project.
Jenna L: For network, ask for higher ephemeral external IP limit in that region or plan NAT egress — we had exhaustion last quarter.
Priya S: Created ticket #GCP-3821: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=my-project&ticket=GCP-3821 — added the reservations plan and cost estimate. Noted PD IOPS and external IP.
Alex R: Thanks. Next: capacity reservation handoff. Once GCP approves, who will run the reservation commands and confirm instances show as 'reserved'?
Li W: I'll run the reservation commands and validate with `gcloud compute reservations describe bringup-reserve --zone=ap-southeast1-a` and `gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels.bringup-reserve=true'`. I'll also create a short playbook for the on-call engineer.
Mateo C: Validation checklist suggestions: 1) Launch test Jupyter on a reserved A100 node; 2) Push 30-min mixed workload for perf; 3) Verify KV cache priming works across pods; 4) Run autoscaler stress so it respects reservations.
Alex R: Add an acceptance gate: latency SLO < 120ms p50 for the internal perf test and no OOMs during the 30-min run. If fails, fallback plan = route low-priority inference to eu-west1.
Priya S: Finance approved provisional spend for the 30-day reservation window. @finance: thanks! :tada:
capacity-bot: Capacity reservation created (pending approval) — tracking id cap-1805-apse1. Updates will be posted here.
Jenna L: Once reservations are active I'll coordinate the canary rollout with product. Plan is a 2-hour canary then scale to full.
Li W: After creating reservations I'll push a status message here with timestamps and the reservation IDs, and attach the quick commands to revoke if something goes wrong.
Alex R: Great. If anyone hits quota blockers or GCP asks for additional justification ping me directly. Otherwise we'll reconvene here when cap-1805-apse1 is approved. :thumbsup:
